learn.intro: Counting, math and comparing dates are weak spots for Jev: it reads and judges, it does not calculate. The fix is to let Jev judge small pieces and let plain code do the counting and comparing.

compare.title: Jev, asked directly
points: Asked for a count, or which date is first, in one answer
Judges well, but does not calculate

compare.title: An LLM, asked directly
points: Answers the same question in a fixed JSON format
Pays for every token it writes

compare.title: Jev + Code
points: Jev answers one small question per entry, or reads each date part
Code adds up the yes answers, or compares the dates
The counting is exact, because code did it

predict.intro: On the Play step, Jev and an LLM are asked straight out how many entries in a list are fruits (4 lists), and which of two dates comes first (4 pairs). After that you see the fix, where Jev only judges small pieces and code does the counting. For now, guess about the direct questions only.

questions.prompt: Asked directly, who gets more of the 8 counting and date questions right?

tasks.title: Count the fruits: after the fix
Which date is first: asked directly
Which date is first: after the fix

why: Asked directly, each racer has to count or compare inside a single answer. Jev judges well but does not calculate, and the fruit counts show where it slips. The four date pairs here were easy enough for every racer, but a direct answer still comes with no guarantee.
After the fix, Jev only answers small judgments: is this entry a fruit, what is the day of this date. Code does the adding and the comparing, so the arithmetic cannot go wrong.
Keep counting, math and dates in code. Use Jev for the judgments code can't make.

questions.prompt: In the fix, which part should do the counting and the date comparing?

options.text: In plain code, after Jev answers the small questions
Inside Jev, in one bigger question

questions.explanation: Code does arithmetic and comparisons exactly, every time. Jev is for the judgments around them, like whether an entry is a fruit or what day a date names.

questions.prompt: In the fix, what does Jev answer?

options.text: Small judgments: one yes or no per entry, or one part of a date
The final count or the final order

questions.explanation: Jev handles each small judgment, which is what it is good at. The code then combines those answers into the count or the order.
